The Region of Lower Extremity.
The lower extremity is divided into
• Regio glutea.
• Regio femoris et genu.
• Regio cruris.
• Regio talocruralis et pedis.


--- Slide/Halaman 3 ---
The muscles of regio Glutea
Muscle of gluteal region are divided into two groups:
•
Pars Profundus : mostly act as latero( exo) rotator of the femur.
– M. piriformis.
– M. obturator internus.
– M. gamellus superior.
– M. gamellus inferior.
– M. quadratus femoris.
•
Pars superficialis : mostly act as abductor and extensor of the femur.
– M. gluteus medius.
– M. gluteus minimus.
– M. gluteus maximus.
– M. tensor fascia latae.

n. gluteus superior :

– m. gluteus minimus.
– M. tensor fascia latae.

--- Slide/Halaman 8 ---
THE FORAMEN ISCHIADICUM MAJUS 
( GREATER SCIATIC FORAMEN)
• is formed on the posterolateral pelvic wall and is the major 
route for structures to pass between the pelvis and regio 
glutea of extremitas inferior.
• The margin :
Incisura ischiadica major.
Lig. Sacrospinosum and sacrotuberosum.
Lateral border of the sacrum
• Divisions :
m. piriformis passes through the foramen ischiadicum and
divide the foramen into
foramen suprapiriformis; superior to the muscle and 
foramen infrapiriformis; inferior to the muscle.

--- Slide/Halaman 12 ---
VASCULARISATION OF THE GLUTEA
• The arteries of the regio glutea come from 
– a. glutea superior and 
– a. glutea inferior. 
The a. glutea superior enter the regio glutea from 
pelvic cavity through foramen suprapiriformis, and a. 
glutea inferior through foramen infrapiriformis. They 
have collateral anastomose with branches of a. 
femoralis.
• The veins follow the the arteries into pelvis  
where they join the pelvic plexus.

ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT
•
Extensor muscle at the knee joint :
– M. sartorius
– M. quadriceps femoris (m. rectus femoris,vastus 
lateralis, vastus intermedius and vastus medialis).
•
Innervated by branch of N. femoralis  


--- Slide/Halaman 22 ---
POSTERIOR COMPARTMENT
• Contains muscle that mainly extend hip at hip joint, and 
flex the leg at knee joint
• Hamstring’muscle ie.
• M. biceps femoris.
• M. semitendinosus.
• M. semimembranosus.
• All the muscle of posterior compartment are innervated by 
n. ischiadicus


--- Slide/Halaman 23 ---
MEDIAL COMPARTMENT
•
Contains the muscle that mainly adduct the hip at hip joint.ie.
• M. gracilis.
• M. pectineus.
• M.adductor magnus.
• M. adductor longus.
• M. adductor brevis.
• M. obturator externus.
•
All the muscle of medial compartment except the hamstring part of 
m adductor magnus are innervated by n. obturatorius. 
•
The hamstrings part of m adductor magnus are innervated by n. 
ischiadicus.


--- Slide/Halaman 24 ---
Fascia lata.
• Fascia lata is the deep fascia of the lower 
extremity, that covers the limb.
• Fascia lata has one rominent aperture on the 
anterior aspect of the thigh, just inferior to 
medial end og lig. inginalis this aperture is 
called saphenous opening or fossa ovalis.

FEMORAL TRIANGLE ( TRIGONUM FEMORALIS )
• The trigonum femoralis is a wedge-shaped depression, 
formed by muscle on anterior suprface of the thigh.
• The margin of triangle are.
• Cranially
:lig. Inguinalis.
• Medially
:medial margin of m. adductor longus.
• Laterally
:medial margin of m. sartorius.
• The floor 
:fossa iliopectinea.
• The apex point inferiorly and continuous with canalis 
adductorius.

• Superficial group :

• Insertion : calcaneus throuh lig. Achilles.

to propel body forward during walking and running and can

The Veins Of The Lower Extremity
Veins draining the lower extremity from superficial and 
deeps groups.
The deep veins generally follow the arteries.
The superficial veins form 2 major channels.
V. saphena magna.
V. saphena parva.
